title: Gapped-Scalar Dispersion Positivity and Finite Bootstrap

items.title: Gapped identical-scalar forward-amplitude data
items.design_state: Exact conditional input package for a gapped identical-scalar forward amplitude, including crossing, pole subtraction, real analyticity, growth, and spectral-sign assumptions.
items.statement:
Use natural units $c=\hbar=1$ and metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. An external scalar datum consists of a spin-zero species assigned a mass $m>0$ and elastic two-particle threshold $s=4m^2$. This is a mathematical input package; it does not construct a one-particle scattering state or a scattering matrix. For real on-shell momenta $p_1,p_2$ incoming and $p_3,p_4$ outgoing, with $p_j^2=-m^2$ and $p_1+p_2=p_3+p_4$, define

$$s=-(p_1+p_2)^2,\qquad t=-(p_1-p_3)^2,\qquad u=-(p_1-p_4)^2.$$

Then $s+t+u=4m^2$. The forward slice is the complex-valued function $A(s)=\mathcal A(s,0,4m^2-s)$ obtained by analytically continuing the identical-scalar $2\to2$ amplitude to $t=0$. The crossing action on this slice is $s\mapsto4m^2-s$, which exchanges $s$ and $u$. Assume $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$ wherever both sides are defined.

For context, define the physical elastic kinematic region

$$\mathscr P_m=\{(s,t,u)\in\mathbb R^3:s>4m^2,\;-(s-4m^2)\le t\le0,\;u=4m^2-s-t\}.$$

When supplied, the full physical amplitude is a map $\mathcal A_{\mathrm{phys}}:\mathscr P_m\to\mathbb C$; its analytic continuation used in the forward data above is a separate supplied part of the input, with upper boundary value $A(s+i0)=\mathcal A_{\mathrm{phys}}(s,0,4m^2-s)$ for $s>4m^2$. For $(s,t,u)\in\mathscr P_m$, put $x=1+2t/(s-4m^2)\in[-1,1]$. For each integer $\ell\ge0$, define the normalized Legendre polynomial $P_\ell:\mathbb C\to\mathbb C$ by

$$P_\ell(x)=\frac{1}{2^\ell\ell!}\frac{d^\ell}{dx^\ell}(x^2-1)^\ell,$$

and let $a_\ell:(4m^2,\infty)\to\mathbb C$ be the complex partial-wave coefficient function in this channel. When a full partial-wave expansion is asserted on the physical angular interval, require the partial sums of the right-hand side below to converge uniformly in $x\in[-1,1]$ for each fixed $s>4m^2$ to the supplied physical amplitude. Use the normalization

$$\mathcal A_{\mathrm{phys}}(s,t,u)=16\pi\sqrt{\frac{s}{s-4m^2}}\sum_{\ell=0}^{\infty}(2\ell+1)P_\ell\!\left(1+\frac{2t}{s-4m^2}\right)a_\ell(s),\qquad P_\ell(1)=1.$$

For the forward sign alone, convergence of the series at $x=1$ suffices. The downstream forward-positivity result uses the optical-theorem sign $\operatorname{Im}A(s+i0)\ge0$ for $s>4m^2$ as input; a full partial-wave realization is not inferred from this definition. In the displayed normalization, the sign follows if the forward series converges and the supplied partial waves obey $\operatorname{Im}a_\ell(s)\ge|a_\ell(s)|^2\ge0$ for every $s>4m^2$ and every $\ell$.

Put $\nu_0=2m^2$ and $v=s-2m^2$, so $u-2m^2=-v$. Choose finitely many real numbers $p_j\in(0,4m^2)\setminus\{2m^2\}$ and real residues $r_j$, and set

$$P(s)=\sum_j\left(\frac{r_j}{s-p_j}+\frac{r_j}{4m^2-p_j-s}\right).$$

Each summand pair is the real simple-pole principal part at $s=p_j$ and its $s\leftrightarrow u$ crossing partner; hence $P(4m^2-s)=P(s)$. These poles lie off the two-particle cuts. Define the pole-subtracted forward function $B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v)$. Assume $B$ is holomorphic on

$$\Omega_{\nu_0}=\mathbb C\setminus\bigl((-\infty,-\nu_0]\cup[\nu_0,\infty)\bigr),$$

real analytic there, meaning $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$, and has finite upper and lower boundary values on both cuts except at their endpoints. Here the two-particle gap is the open interval $(-\nu_0,\nu_0)$ in the $v$ variable; no massless pole or cut reaches the forward point $t=0$.

Require additionally that $B$ extends continuously from each open half-plane onto every compact segment of either real cut bank avoiding $\pm\nu_0$. This is an extra admissibility assumption on the supplied data, not a consequence of finite pointwise boundary values or a claim about every quantum field theory. 

Assume the exact high-energy condition $B(w)=o(|w|^2)$ uniformly as $|w|\to\infty$ in the closed upper half-plane, including upper cut-bank limits. In particular this holds on the large upper semicircles after any fixed bounded horizontal translation. For $\nu\ge\nu_0$, define the absorptive density $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}B(\nu+i0)$. Require $\rho$ to be nonnegative and Riemann integrable on every compact subinterval of $[\nu_0,\infty)$, and require $\int_{\nu_0}^{\infty}\rho(\nu)\nu^{-3}\,d\nu$ to converge as a finite improper Riemann integral. For every real $v$ with $|v|<\nu_0$, require the integrals along both sides of the two cuts of $[B(x)-B(0)]/[x^2(x-v)]$, with boundary values taken from the upper and lower half-planes, to exist as finite improper Riemann limits. Require also that the small endpoint arcs at $\pm\nu_0$ for this integrand vanish in the contour limit. Since $P$ is real off its poles, $\rho(\nu)=\operatorname{Im}A(2m^2+\nu+i0)$ for $\nu>\nu_0$ on the right cut.

The normalized forward Taylor coefficients are $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ for integers $n\ge1$. They have units $(\text{mass})^{-4n}$; $\nu_0$ has units $(\text{mass})^2$. No sign is assigned here to a generic off-shell Lagrangian coefficient.

items.title: Crossing evenness at the scalar subtraction point
items.design_state: Direct proof that the specified pole-subtracted forward function is even and has vanishing first derivative at the subtraction point.
items.statement: Let $m>0$, let $A(s)$ be the forward slice of identical-scalar amplitude data satisfying $A(s)=A(4m^2-s)$, and let $P(s)$ be a finite sum of isolated simple real pole principal parts in $0<s<4m^2$ and their $s\leftrightarrow u$ crossing partners, satisfying $P(s)=P(4m^2-s)$. Put $B(v)=A(2m^2+v)-P(2m^2+v)$ wherever these expressions are defined. Then $B(-v)=B(v)$. If $B$ is complex differentiable in a neighbourhood of $v=0$, then $B'(0)=0$.

items.title: Finite truncated forward-amplitude bootstrap data
items.design_state: Exact finite normalized on-shell coefficient vector and three stated families of necessary quadratic positivity tests.
items.statement:
Let $B(v)$ and $\nu_0=2m^2>0$ be the pole-subtracted forward-amplitude data of the amplitude-input definition. In addition to being even and holomorphic near $v=0$, retain its real-analyticity condition $B(\overline v)=\overline{B(v)}$. If $B(v)=\sum_{j\ge0}\beta_jv^j$ near $0$, uniqueness of the Taylor expansion gives $\beta_j=\overline{\beta_j}$ from this condition and $\beta_{2n+1}=0$ from evenness. Hence the even Taylor coefficients are real. Fix an integer truncation order $N\ge1$. For $n\ge1$ define the Taylor coefficient $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ and the dimensionless forward on-shell coefficient $b_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}c_{k+1}\in\mathbb R$ for $0\le k\le N$. Since $v$ and $\nu_0$ have units $(\text{mass})^2$, $c_n$ has units $(\text{mass})^{-4n}$ and $b_k$ is dimensionless. Here “Wilson coefficient” refers only to this normalized on-shell amplitude coordinate; it does not identify a generic coefficient of an off-shell Lagrangian operator basis.

For each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r\le N$, form the quadratic constraint

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j}\ge0\qquad\text{for every }(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}.$$

For each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r+1\le N$, form the two additional quadratic constraints

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j+1}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j\bigl(b_{i+j}-b_{i+j+1}\bigr)\ge0\qquad\text{for every }(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}.$$

The **finite order-$N$ forward-amplitude bootstrap feasible set** $\mathcal K_N$ is the subset of $\mathbb R^{N+1}$ consisting of vectors $(b_0,\ldots,b_N)$ that satisfy every applicable constraint above. The finite truncated bootstrap problem is to determine whether a supplied coefficient vector belongs to $\mathcal K_N$. Passing this finite test is a necessary condition supplied by forward positivity; it is not defined to be sufficient for the existence of a full amplitude-data package as defined above.

items.title: Finite truncated forward-positivity constraints
items.design_state: Derives all finite Hankel and interval-localizer inequalities from the positive spectral moment representation.
items.statement:
For any gapped identical-scalar forward-amplitude data satisfying all the defined analytic, continuous-bank, endpoint and growth conditions, with $m>0$, gap $
u_0=2m^2$, an even pole-subtracted function $B$ and nonnegative density $ho(
u)=\operatorname{Im}B(
u+i0)$ for $
u>
u_0$, extended by $ho(
u_0)=0$, with finite $\int_{
u_0}^{\infty}ho(
u)
u^{-3}\,d
u$, let $c_n=B^{(2n)}(0)/(2n)!$ and $b_k=
u_0^{2k+2}c_{k+1}$. For every integer $N\ge1$, the vector $(b_0,\ldots,b_N)$ belongs to the finite feasible set $\mathcal K_N$ defined by the following quadratic inequalities: for each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r\le N$ and every $(a_0,\ldots,a_r)\in\mathbb R^{r+1}$,

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j}\ge0,$$

and for each integer $r\ge0$ with $2r+1\le N$ and every such vector,

$$\sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j b_{i+j+1}\ge0,\qquad \sum_{i,j=0}^{r}a_i a_j(b_{i+j}-b_{i+j+1})\ge0.$$

These are necessary finite positivity tests on normalized forward on-shell amplitude coordinates. Membership in $\mathcal K_N$ is not asserted to be sufficient for a full amplitude or a physical quantum field theory.

items.title: Quartic scalar contact jets descend through verified operator relations
items.design_state: Explicit bounded quartic polarization map on the verified-relation image of the existing finite operator quotient; contact coefficient and exact-remainder interface, not arbitrary quantum matching.
items.statement:
Fix $m>0$, $\Lambda>0$, integers $r\ge1$, $D\ge4$ and $N\ge1$, and the metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Use the finite-jet operator quotient $\mathcal Q_D=V_D/R_D$ for one commuting scalar $\phi$ of weight one, field-degree cutoff four, derivative cutoff $r$, and complex orthogonal spacetime-index action preserving $\eta$. Let $U_D\subset V_D$ be the subspace of degree-exactly-four scalar polynomials whose indices are contracted using $\eta$ only, and let $Q_D^{(4)}$ be its image in $\mathcal Q_D$. Thus $Q_D^{(4)}=U_D/(U_D\cap R_D)$; operators outside this image are not assigned a contact map. Fix the monomial basis in the commuting jet generators used to write these polynomials. Let $U_{D,\mathbb R}\subset U_D$ consist of the polynomials whose coefficients in that basis are real, and define $Q_{D,\mathbb R}^{(4)}$ to be the image of $U_{D,\mathbb R}$ in $Q_D^{(4)}$. This is the chosen real subspace of classes admitting a coefficientwise-real representative; no conjugation structure on the full complex quotient is presumed.

Require the following certificate for the actual declared relations: every $H\in U_D\cap R_D$ is a finite sum of identically zero jet polynomials, total divergences $\partial_\mu J^\mu$ with $J$ quartic, and $F(\Box-m^2)\phi$ with $F$ cubic, where $\Box=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu\partial_\nu$. The summands may use a larger finite jet space and different engineering weights; their polynomial sum must equal $H$ before any on-shell substitution. This is an additional restriction on the selected $R_D$, not a claim about an arbitrary relation subspace or its completeness.

For $O\in U_D$ introduce commuting indeterminates $z_1,\ldots,z_4$ and complex four-vectors $k_1,\ldots,k_4$. Its polarized Fourier vertex is

$$T_O(k_1,k_2,k_3,k_4)=[z_1z_2z_3z_4]\,O\!\left(\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_a}\phi\mapsto\sum_{j=1}^4 z_j i^a k_{j,\mu_1}\cdots k_{j,\mu_a}\right).$$

The coefficient convention contains no $1/4!$. Impose $\sum_jk_j=0$, $k_j^2=-m^2$, and set $s=-(k_1+k_2)^2$, $t=-(k_1+k_3)^2$, $u=-(k_1+k_4)^2$. Replace contracted products by $k_j^2=-m^2$, $k_1\cdot k_2=k_3\cdot k_4=m^2-s/2$, $k_1\cdot k_3=k_2\cdot k_4=m^2-t/2$, and $k_1\cdot k_4=k_2\cdot k_3=m^2-u/2$. Put $t=0$, $s=2m^2+v$, $u=2m^2-v$, obtaining a polynomial $t_O(v)$. Define $\nu_0=2m^2$ and the linear contact-jet map

$$M_{D,N}([O])_k=\nu_0^{2k+2}\Lambda^{4-D}[v^{2k+2}]t_O(v),\qquad 0\le k\le N.$$

Then this map $Q_D^{(4)}\to\mathbb C^{N+1}$ is well-defined and $t_O$ is even. Its restriction to $Q_{D,\mathbb R}^{(4)}$ takes values in $\mathbb R^{N+1}$. For $D=8$, $O_8=(\partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phi)^2$ satisfies, for every $C_8\in\mathbb R$,

$$t_{O_8}(v)=8m^4+4v^2,\qquad M_{8,N}([C_8O_8])=(4\nu_0^2C_8/\Lambda^4,0,\ldots,0).$$

In particular the coefficient $[v^2]\Lambda^{-4}t_{C_8O_8}=4C_8/\Lambda^4$ is invariant under the certified relations. On $Q_{D,\mathbb R}^{(4)}$, the real target coordinates use precisely the normalized convention of the finite forward-amplitude bootstrap problem. This algebraic map describes one quartic contact insertion about the free massive scalar quadratic action. It does not equate the contact polynomial to an exact full amplitude, discard loop or other-operator contributions, or infer positivity of a perturbative term from positivity of a full amplitude.

references.title: Juan Carlos Criado and Manuel Pérez-Victoria, Field redefinitions in effective theories at higher orders

items.title: Allowed and excluded order-two forward coefficients
items.design_state: Checks one order-two candidate in the finite feasible set and exhibits a candidate excluded by a negative Hankel quadratic form.
items.statement: At truncation order $N=2$, let $(b_0,b_1,b_2)$ denote the normalized forward on-shell amplitude coordinates and let $\mathcal K_2$ be the finite feasible set defined by the order-two constraints. The strict region $\mathcal U_2=\{b_0>0,\ b_1>0,\ b_0-b_1>0,\ b_0b_2-b_1^2>0\}$ is contained in $\mathcal K_2$. The strict region $\mathcal V_2=\{b_0>0,\ b_1>0,\ b_0-b_1>0,\ b_0b_2-b_1^2<0\}$ is disjoint from $\mathcal K_2$. The vectors $b^{\mathrm{pass}}=(1,\tfrac12,\tfrac13)\in\mathcal U_2$ and $b^{\mathrm{fail}}=(1,\tfrac12,\tfrac18)\in\mathcal V_2$ witness that both regions are nonempty. The first region passes the finite necessary test; this example does not assert that any vector passing that test extends to full analytic amplitude data or a physical theory, and it assigns no sign to a generic off-shell Lagrangian coefficient.
